lists.of: a question about whether something could be an illusion and what causes it
items: 29. Could the absolute independence of events (of any physical events in the cosmos) : be an illusion caused by : wanton desire?
30. Could transcendental or eternal ideas : be an illusion caused by : logical fallacies or misapplication of general principles?
31. Could absolutely fundamental things : be an illusion caused by : homology of perceptual categories?
32. Could "physical separability" : be an illusion caused by : reification or hypostatization?
33. Could logical neutrality of human languages : be an illusion caused by : expectation?
34. Could physical-mental heterousia : be an illusion caused by : reliance on a single system?
35. Could irreconcilable opposites : be an illusion caused by : false or inadequate world view?
36. Could progress : be an illusion caused by : equivalence?
37. Could space as merely 3-dimensional : be an illusion caused by : information overload, mental or perceptual fatigue, or 'environmental burial'?
38. Could the 'state-specificity' of society (as opposed to a fundamental indeterminacy, or intrinsic and irreducible ambiguity, of its would-be 'states') : be an illusion caused by : complexity?
39. Could that some things are truly impossible : be an illusion caused by : 'pan-truth' (misapplication of the doctrine so-named) or pan-paradoxy?
40. Could the knowledgeability of "experts" : be an illusion caused by : neuropsychological heredity (e.g., inherited modes, gestalten, or elements of perception, thought, feeling, or action)?
41. Could the chaotic appearance of civilization : be an illusion caused by : untrained or undisciplined perception?

42. Could the stability of the solar system : be an illusion caused by : neglect of scientific procedures (testing, experimentation, prediction, validation, reproduction, statistical evaluation, induction, deduction, rich hypothecation, etc)?
43. Could morphological complexity : be an illusion caused by : arbitrary decisions?
44. Could that anything is final : be an illusion caused by : camouflage, hiding, or 'environmental mimicry or assimilation'?
45. Could absolute shape or structural order (self-structure) : be an illusion caused by : simplism?
46. Could the running down of the universe : be an illusion caused by : confusion of form and content?
47. Could the existence of only one 4-dimensional spacetime : be an illusion caused by : absence of a touchstone?
48. Could the divisibility of reality : be an illusion caused by : confusion?
49. Could multitudes of copies or types of particles (as opposed to a 'single-particle' cosmos) : be an illusion caused by : conceptual poverty?
50. Could eternal laws : be an illusion caused by : absence of a touchstone?
51. Could 'human intelligence' : be an illusion caused by : misdescription, under-description, or under-perception?

52. Could Aristotelian 2-valued logic (absolute truth-or-falsehood) : be an illusion caused by : overgeneralization, exaggeration, infinitization, absolutization, non-qualification, eternalization, idealization, etc?
53. Could the necessity of one's own existence : be an illusion caused by : panintertransformability?
54. Could self : be an illusion caused by : continuity?
55. Could absolute truth : be an illusion caused by : misrepresentation or mistreatment?
56. Could unique probability : be an illusion caused by : perceptual or mental expedience?
57. Could the concreteness (as opposed to abstractness) of consciousness : be an illusion caused by : personification or self-projection?
58. Could absolute laws : be an illusion caused by : multidimensionality?
59. Could the self-existence of external reality : be an illusion caused by : conceptual poverty?
60. Could the cosmic importance of man : be an illusion caused by : discontinuity?
61. Could phenotypal monogenicity : be an illusion caused by : misclassification or misidentification?

62. Could complex causes : be an illusion caused by : ignorance about illusion in general (its diversity, categories, taxa, omnipresence, signs, causes, genesis, laws, instances and spectrum of exemplifications, transformations, transcendence, degrees, related phenomena, powers, etc)?
63. Could measurable intelligence : be an illusion caused by : cooperative phenomena or interdependences?
64. Could unevolved cosmogonic entities : be an illusion caused by : excessive abstraction, theoretical fictions, or neglect of concrete facts?
65. Could different sciences : be an illusion caused by : inexperience or naivete?

notes: The title and preceding entries are outside the photograph. Entry 66 is cut off at the bottom and omitted.
